summary: Merge sort splits an array in half, sorts each half recursively, and merges the two sorted halves. It runs in O(n log n) time on every input.
notes: scores.slice(0, mid) and scores.slice(mid) make new arrays, so mergeSort returns a new array and leaves the original alone.
left[i] <= right[j] uses <= so equal scores keep their original order. That makes the sort stable.
result.push(...left.slice(i), ...right.slice(j)) copies the leftovers after one side runs out.
pitfall: Forgetting the base case if (scores.length <= 1) makes the function call itself forever and ends with RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
contrast: JavaScript's slice() copies part of an array like a Python slice, so this version matches Python's and returns a new array. Java usually passes index ranges and sorts in place to avoid copying.
